Calculate the number-average molecular weight (M_n) of the polymer sample using the given molecular-weight distribution.
Use the formula M_n = Σ(N_i × M_i) / Σ(N_i), where N_i is the number of molecules (chain count) at each molecular weight M_i.
Treat the values 56526, 92809, 115856, and 126029 g/mol as the molecular weights M_i.
Treat the values 96, 131, 153, and 146 as the corresponding number of molecules N_i at each weight.
Compute Σ(N_i × M_i) = (96 × 56526) + (131 × 92809) + (153 × 115856) + (146 × 126029) = 53,710,677 g/mol.
Compute Σ(N_i) = 96 + 131 + 153 + 146 = 526.
Divide to obtain M_n = 53,710,677 / 526 ≈ 102,112 g/mol.
Report the final result as M_n ≈ 102,112 g/mol (approximately 102,111.55 g/mol).
Do not compute any weight-average or other molecular-weight averages; only M_n is required.
Present the answer in g/mol.
